correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the distributional stationary Neumann Green kernel, its zero-integral homogeneous flux correction, both boundary derivatives, the membrane law and boundary densities; derived I=(s h/g)(1-u)atanh(h u) exactly. For 0<h<1, F_h(0)>0>F_h(1) and F_h prime=-2h(1-h^2u)/(1-h^2u^2)^2<0 give the unique global maximizer. At the root, artanh(h u)>h u gives positive F_h parameter derivative and hence strict optimizer ordering. The limits h->0 and h->1 yield sharp universal endpoints; point-reset families approach both bounds. A standard-library verifier passed 302 independent finite diagnostics including numerical boundary flux/PDE/normalization, scans and constants. Finite testing does not establish infinite uniqueness, which rests on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 source provides the membrane BVP, entropy formula and plotted nonmonotonicity but not uniqueness or a closed universal optimization law. The independently checked local prior determines a rate-dependent membrane flux and identifiable reset asymmetry, not the global nonlinear entropy-permeability optimizer. A direct Neumann-resolvent reduction and strict derivative analysis establish exactly one maximizer for every Borel reset law with nonzero current, plus monotonic asymmetry and sharp universal bounds. Searches found no covering named theorem. General conductance-optimization literature remains a publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: Membrane permeability is the natural controllable parameter in semipermeable transport. The source demonstrates nonmonotone interfacial entropy versus permeability but cannot tell from plots whether several optimal barriers are possible. The result gives a complete all-Borel-source optimizer classification, a sharp dimensionless impedance-matching band independent of the reset law, and a strict trend with source asymmetry, directly relevant to interpreting stationary dissipation. It is not merely an arbitrary parameter slice or a restatement of nonmonotonicity. It does not claim optimization of total entropy or a physical extremum principle.
